- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope sharply in next 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is high but price is trending down; adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment >0.7 and price drops >1%.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model often overfits recent noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
